sec: Drugs causing AKI: four-column classification · p798

items.q: Match each drug class with its column in the drug-induced AKI chart — 1) NSAIDs  2) Vancomycin and aminoglycosides  3) Methotrexate and indinavir  4) PPIs and beta-lactams … A) AIN  B) Pre-renal failure  C) ATN  D) Intratubular obstruction (oliguric AKI)
items.exp: Drug chart: pre-renal failure — NSAIDs, drugs causing ↑Ca²⁺, ACEi/ARB, calcineurin inhibitors; ATN — vancomycin, aminoglycosides, amphotericin B, cisplatin, ethylene glycol, salicylates; intratubular obstruction (oliguric AKI) — methotrexate (increased dose), indinavir, triamterene, acyclovir, sulfonamides; AIN — PPIs, beta-lactams, rifampicin, allopurinol and anticonvulsants (also NSAIDs and diuretics). (Book p798)

items.q: All but one of the following drugs cause ATN. Which is the odd one out?
items.exp: Triamterene is grouped under intratubular obstruction (oliguric AKI) along with methotrexate, indinavir, acyclovir and sulfonamides; vancomycin, aminoglycosides, amphotericin B and cisplatin belong to ATN. (Book p798)

items.q: Match the mnemonic letters in the ATN column — 1) V  2) A  3) C  4) E … A) Ethylene glycol (oxalate urine crystals)  B) Vancomycin  C) Aminoglycosides, adefovir, amphotericin B  D) Cisplatin, cyclophosphamide, cidofovir
items.exp: ATN mnemonic: V — vancomycin; A — aminoglycosides, adefovir, amphotericin B; C — cisplatin, cyclophosphamide, cidofovir; E — ethylene glycol (oxalate urine crystals); S — salicylates. (Book p798)

items.q: A patient with ethylene glycol poisoning has oxalate crystals in the urine. In the drug chart, ethylene glycol is classified under:
items.exp: Ethylene glycol is listed in the ATN column with the annotation 'oxalate urine crystals'. (Book p798)

items.q: Match the mnemonic letters in the intratubular obstruction column — 1) m  2) I  3) T  4) A  5) S … A) Methotrexate (increased dose)  B) Indinavir  C) Triamterene  D) Acyclovir  E) Sulfonamides
items.exp: Intratubular obstruction (oliguric AKI) mnemonic: m — methotrexate (increased dose); I — indinavir; T — triamterene; A — acyclovir; S — sulfonamides. (Book p798)

items.q: Match the AIN column drugs — 1) PPIs  2) β lactams  3) Rifampicin  4) Allopurinol and anticonvulsants  5) NSAIDs and diuretics … A) All appear in the AIN column
opts: All are listed in the AIN column
Only PPIs and beta-lactams are in the AIN column
Only allopurinol is in the AIN column
None is in the AIN column
items.exp: AIN column: PPIs; β lactams; rifampicin; allopurinol, anticonvulsants; and NSAIDs, diuretics — remembered by the mnemonic. (Book p798)

items.q: A patient started on indinavir for HIV develops oliguric AKI. The mechanism in the drug chart is:
items.exp: Indinavir is listed in the intratubular obstruction column, which is described as oliguric AKI. (Book p798)

items.q: NSAIDs appear in the drug chart both as a pre-renal cause and in the AIN column.
opts: False — NSAIDs appear only as a pre-renal cause
False — NSAIDs appear only under ATN
items.exp: NSAIDs are listed under pre-renal failure and again in the AIN column (with diuretics), reflecting their dual mechanisms. (Book p798)

items.q: All but one of the following drugs cause intratubular obstruction. Which is the odd one out?
items.exp: Adefovir is in the ATN column (with aminoglycosides and amphotericin B); methotrexate, acyclovir, sulfonamides and triamterene cause intratubular obstruction. (Book p798)

items.q: Which drug group is listed under pre-renal failure as causing ↑serum calcium in the drug chart?
items.exp: Pre-renal failure column: NSAIDs; drugs causing ↑Ca²⁺ (hypercalcemia); ACEi/ARB; calcineurin inhibitors. (Book p798)
